question: How many sons did Absalom have?
summary: 2 Samuel 14:27 says three sons were born to Absalom. 2 Samuel 18:18 has Absalom himself saying he has no son to keep his name in remembrance, which is why he set up a memorial pillar. Both statements appear in the same book about the same person.

reconcile.connective: The standard harmonization holds the three sons died young, so by the time Absalom raised his pillar he genuinely had no son left to keep his name.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is pressed by Steve Wells in the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, whose own "How many sons did Absalom have?" entry pairs these verses as a flat contradiction: 14:27 reports three sons, yet 18:18 has Absalom say he has none.

pd_work.note: Gill treats this exact pair at 14:27, reconciling the three sons with 18:18 by the sons' early death. Used as the PD anchor because Haley's coverage of this specific verse-pair could not be confirmed; the same 'sons died young' reading is run by Keil & Delitzsch, Clarke, and the Tyndale notes.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Who very probably died young; and the rather it may be thought so, since their names are not given, and more especially since it is said that Absalom had no sons, and therefore erected a pillar to keep up the remembrance of his name; unless it can be thought that that was set up before he had any sons, which is not so likely …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill names the harmonizing mechanism directly: the three sons of 14:27 died young, which is why Absalom (18:18) says he has no son and erects a memorial pillar. Cross-references Sa2 18:18 explicitly.
excerpts.source_note_text:
And unto Absalom there were born three sons,.... Who very probably died young; and the rather it may be thought so, since their names are not given, and more especially since it is said that Absalom had no sons, and therefore erected a pillar to keep up the remembrance of his name; unless it can be thought that that was set up before he had any sons, which is not so likely; see Sa2 18:18,
and one daughter, whose name was Tamar; and whom he named after his sister Tamar, who was ravished by Amnon; the Septuagint version in some copies adds,"and she became the wife of Rehoboam, the son of Solomon, and bore to him Abia;''and so says Josephus (b); see Kg1 15:22,
she was a woman of a fair countenance; as was her aunt, after whom she was named, Sa2 13:1; by this it appears that she lived to a woman's estate, though the sons of Absalom died young.
(b) Ut supra. (Antiqu. l. 7. c. 8. sect. 5.)
